justifications.functional_suitability: All requirements (R-01 to R-04) are directly addressed by dedicated components: WebRTC Video Module and Consultation Session Manager for video, E-Prescription Dispatcher for prescriptions, AI Triage Service for symptom checking, and Consent Ledger Manager for patient consent.
justifications.performance_efficiency: The design incorporates GCP Cloud CDN, local-first offline caching in Cross-Platform UI Layer, gRPC between internal services, and Rate Limiting & Resilience Proxy, effectively optimizing edge latency and resource consumption.
justifications.compatibility: Pharmacy Client supports HL7 FHIR and REST for external healthcare interoperability, and OIDC/SAML integrates regional identity providers. However, explicit adapters for divergent national EU e-prescription standards are not detailed.
justifications.usability: Patients and clinicians are well served via Web & Mobile Apps built in Flutter/React, featuring low-bandwidth adaptations in WebRTC Video Module and offline caching in Cross-Platform UI Layer for rural users.
justifications.reliability: Resilience is reinforced by Dispatch Engine's idempotent routing, session state recovery in Consultation Session Manager, and degraded video below 300 kbit/s. However, regional failover and database disaster recovery mechanisms are not fully detailed.
justifications.security: Consent Enforcement Interceptor, PHI Sanitizer, mTLS, regional data isolation, CMEK Cloud KMS encryption, and immutable logging across Audit Logger and Consent & Audit Ledger satisfy GDPR, HIPAA, and EU MDR accountability.
justifications.maintainability: The architecture shows clean separation of concerns across specialized containers (AI Triage Service, E-Prescription Dispatcher, Core Telehealth Service) and well-scoped components with explicit protocols (gRPC, REST), facilitating testability and independent modification.
justifications.portability: Components use containerized stacks (Go, Spring Boot, FastAPI) deployable to GCP target regions (europe-west3, us-central1). Some coupling exists with GCP-specific services (Cloud SQL, Cloud KMS, Vertex AI), though standard protocols mitigate lock-in.

PERF-01.justification: Signaling and session management are handled by Core Telehealth Service and API Gateway, but backend WebRTC media relays or SFU/TURN servers necessary to sustain 5,000 video streams are absent.
sensitivity_points: Availability of dedicated media routing infrastructure for peer connections
tradeoffs: Peer-to-peer WebRTC reduces infrastructure cost but degrades under restrictive firewalls

PERF-02.justification: A volume of 50,000 requests per hour is approximately 14 RPS, which the Go API Gateway and FastAPI AI Triage Service easily handle with version-pinned Vertex AI inference calls.
sensitivity_points: Inference latency and rate limits on GCP Vertex AI
tradeoffs: Synchronous local PHI sanitization ensures compliance at the cost of processing latency

AVAIL-01.justification: The WebRTC Video Module is explicitly specified to support degraded connections below 300 kbit/s, while the Cross-Platform UI Layer provides resilient local-first state and offline caching.
sensitivity_points: Adaptive bitrate codec negotiation and local-first client caching
tradeoffs: Lowering video quality preserves audio continuity and consultation integrity

AVAIL-02.justification: Only a single US region (us-central1) is defined in the target cloud without an automated multi-region US failover or disaster recovery topology, preventing guaranteed 1-hour recovery without cross-border migration.
sensitivity_points: In-region disaster recovery replication without crossing continental jurisdictions
tradeoffs: Strict regional residency prevents active-active cross-region failover to EU infrastructure

MOD-01.justification: E-Prescription Dispatcher isolates external pharmacy communication in Pharmacy Client, but country-specific adapter plugins or strategy patterns are not explicitly architected to guarantee changes stay confined to one adapter.
sensitivity_points: Modularity and extensibility of national protocol adapters within Pharmacy Client
tradeoffs: A consolidated dispatch container simplifies operations but increases blast radius during adapter updates

MOD-02.justification: The design mandates version-pinned inference APIs to Vertex AI, with Inference Orchestrator and Audit Logger recording model versions and inputs directly to an immutable ledger.
sensitivity_points: Strict version pinning on model endpoints and audit immutability
tradeoffs: Pinning model versions prevents silent drift but requires manual orchestration during rollouts

SEC-01.justification: Consent Enforcement Interceptor validates regional consent prior to executing methods, and all access attempts are captured by Telehealth Notification & Audit Adapter and stored in the encrypted CMEK ledger.
sensitivity_points: Pre-execution authorization interceptors enforcing cross-border data fences
tradeoffs: Per-request cross-region consent checks introduce slight latency on data retrieval

SEC-02.justification: Consent updates and audits are tracked in Consent & Audit Ledger, but research export pipelines, data lakes, or downstream revocation propagation mechanisms are not modeled in the architecture.
sensitivity_points: Propagation latency of consent revocation to secondary data processing systems
tradeoffs: Fine-grained consent ledger updates increase audit fidelity but require downstream sync logic
